title: Exponential de Finetti Theorems for Fermionic Gaussian States
authors: Jędrzej Burkat, Michał Studziński, Sergii Strelchuk
abstract: We prove an exponential variant of the Gaussian de Finetti theorem: the subsystems of permutation-invariant, free-fermionic Gaussian states are well-approximated by convex combinations of almost-i.i.d. states that are Gaussian on subsets of their parts. Our result provides an error bound between the original state and its approximants that decays exponentially in the number of unconstrained parts, becoming super-exponential when the subsystem under consideration is small. The dimensional penalty of our bound is polylogarithmic in the local Hilbert space dimension, an exponential improvement over the standard de Finetti theorem of [Nat. Phys. 3, 645-649]. In the fully i.i.d. limit, our bound recovers the Gaussian de Finetti theorem of [arXiv:2603.12392]. Previous works considered Gaussian-symmetric states, which are supported on the trivial irrep of the tensor matchgate representation. We extend these to a broader class of Gaussian-invariant states containing, for example, i.i.d. copies of single-replica mixed Gaussian states. We show that Gaussian-invariant states are precisely the partial traces of Gaussian-symmetric states on locally enlarged replicas, and always admit a purification into a larger Gaussian-symmetric state. This extends de Finetti theorems to the full set of Gaussian-invariant states, with only a polynomial overhead in the dimensional penalty of the error bound.
summary: This theoretical paper proves an exponential de Finetti theorem tailored for fermionic Gaussian states, significantly improving upon previous bounds. It extends the scope from highly symmetric states to all Gaussian-invariant states by utilizing advanced techniques involving replica symmetry and algebraic identities. The result provides a quantitative measure of how close complex quantum correlations are to simple product states.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove an exponential variant of the de Finetti theorem for free-fermionic Gaussian states, extending previous results from Gaussian-symmetric to the broader class of Gaussian-invariant states.
main_result: They establish that reduced states of Gaussian-invariant fermionic Gaussian states can be approximated by convex combinations of almost-i.i.d. states with an error bound decaying exponentially or super-exponentially in system parameters, achieving polylogarithmic dimensional penalties.
method: The proof combines advanced techniques from quantum information theory, including using Chernoff bounds on overlap variables and establishing algebraic equivalences between different mathematical formulations of the de Finetti theorem via commutation relations involving bridge operators.
model_or_system: The system under study is fermionic Gaussian states defined on a lattice or set of qubits (Hilbert space $H \cong (\mathbb{C}^2)^{\otimes n}$), analyzed through replicas ($k$) and partial traces ($	ext{Tr}_m$). The theory focuses on symmetries like Gaussian-symmetric and Gaussian-invariant states.
key_observables: The primary observable is the error bound $\delta$ quantifying how well a reduced state approximates an i.i.d. mixture; other key elements include overlap variables ($Q$) and bridge operators ($\Lambda_{ab}$).
important_parameters: Key parameters include the number of replicas ($k, m$), the system size ($n$), and the approximation parameter $r$. The analysis highlights different scaling regimes based on the relative sizes of $k$ and $m$.
main_assumptions: The results are derived for free-fermionic Gaussian states and rely heavily on specific algebraic properties involving Majorana operators and parity/pair-parity operators.
figures_summary: Figure 1 numerically compares upper bounds for the error $\delta$ using different mathematical forms (Full Expression, Rising Factorial, Ratio Form) across various regimes of system parameters ($k>m$, $k=m$, $k<m$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the exponential bound for Gaussian-symmetric states (Theorem 1), then extending this to the broader class of Gaussian-invariant states via purification theorems, and finally proving the equivalence between different mathematical formulations of the de Finetti theorem using algebraic identities.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful tools for characterizing entanglement structure in many-body quantum systems by quantifying how close a complex correlated state is to a simple product (i.i.d.) state, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and local measurements in condensed matter physics.
